input.question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".
input.ground_truth: It isn't just "goat cheese", it's just that your average American doesn't have enough experiences with goat cheeses to name any particular one. Feta, Kunik, Castelo Branco, and Clochette are all (at least partially) goat cheese that I've eaten personally. I'd think that pretty much everyone in the US has some experience with feta at a minimum.

Question: Why are there so many different kinds of cheese made from cow's milk, but cheese made from goat's milk is just "goat cheese".

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two types of animal friends: cows and goats.

Cows give a lot of milk, so people have made many different games (or cheeses) with it. They can make cheese that is soft like a hug (brie), hard like a rock (parmesan), or stringy like a necklace (mozzarella). That’s why there are so many names for cow milk cheese.

Goats give less milk, and their milk is a little different. People usually just call the cheese they make from goat milk "goat cheese" because it’s a bit simpler and not as many games have been made with it yet.

So, it’s like having a big box of crayons for cows, but just a few colors for goats!
